q: What are the 3 parts of a fixture function, in order? When does each part run?
a: 1) setup: before the test. 2) await use(value): the test runs during this line. 3) teardown: after the test, even if it failed.

q: Your fixture's teardown runs BEFORE the test (data is already deleted when the test starts). What is the bug?
a: use(value) without await. Write await use(value); so the fixture waits for the test to finish.

browser, context, page: what is each one, and which one holds the cookies?
a: browser = the browser process. context = an isolated 'incognito window' that holds cookies and storage. page = one tab inside a context. New context = new cookies = logged out.

q: Error: Test has unknown parameter "loginPage". What happened?
a: The test asks for a fixture its `test` doesn't have. Usually you imported test from '@playwright/test' instead of from your fixtures file.

q: Name two advantages of fixtures over beforeEach/afterEach.
a: They run only when a test asks for them (lazy); setup and teardown live in one function; the value goes straight into the test; written once and reused in every file.
